text:
sam_customer: Heads up — after upgrading our app to redwood-python 1.26.0 we started seeing doubled API calls for a subset of generation requests and customers reported being charged twice. Anyone else?

maria_support: Oh no. Thanks for reporting. Can you paste a minimal repro and your pip freeze + any request logs you have? Also which API endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings)?

sam_customer: Chat/generate. Attached minimal snippet:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
res = client.chat.generate(model='rwd-llama-7b', prompt='hi', max_tokens=50)
print(res.text)
```
Pip freeze: `redwood-python==1.26.0\nrequests==2.31.0\nurllib3==2.1.0`
Logs show two POSTs within 200ms with identical payload and no Idempotency-Key header. Stack trace points to retry logic in `redwood.http.client` where it does `session.send(...)` twice.

maria_support: Interesting — prior versions added `Idempotency-Key` automatically for chat/generate when retries were enabled. Can you confirm if you set any custom retry config or env vars like `REDWOOD_RETRIES`?

sam_customer: We didn't. Default configuration. We never saw duplicates before the upgrade. Downgrading to 1.25.3 immediately stopped the duplicates.

kevin_engineering: Jumping in — I can repro locally. Quick summary: 1.26.0 introduced a refactor in the transport layer that renamed the internal idempotency attach point. The new code path only adds Idempotency-Key when a `idempotency_key` kwarg is passed explicitly. Previously the SDK generated one for non-streaming mutative calls. So on transient 5xx or connection hiccups the retry loop re-sends the request without idempotency header => duplicate server-side operations and double billing.

kevin_engineering: Repro steps I used:
1) run a tiny mock server that returns 502 on first request then 200 on retry.
2) call the client (no idempotency header)

Mock server output:
```
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] POST /v1/chat/generate -> 502 (first try)
[2026-03-15T18:03:12Z] POST /v1/chat/generate -> 200 (retry)
```
Client logs (redwood debug):
```
DEBUG transport: send attempt 1 -> POST /v1/chat/generate
DEBUG transport: got status 502, scheduling retry
DEBUG transport: send attempt 2 -> POST /v1/chat/generate
```
Note the requests are identical and server saw two executes.

kevin_engineering: Quick curl to mimic the issue (use netcat as server to inspect):
```
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' -v
```
You should see two POSTs when the server sends 502 then 200.

beth_oncall: For mitigation: pin to 1.25.3 or 1.25.x series immediately. As a workaround for 1.26.0 customers can set explicit `headers={"Idempotency-Key": uuid4()}` on mutative requests or disable retries with `client.config.retries = 0` while we patch. Also setting `REDWOOD_DISABLE_RETRIES=true` in env will stop auto-retries.

maria_support: Thanks Kevin. Can you open a short PR to restore auto-idempotency generation for chat/generate and add unit tests against the mock server flow? Also we need a patch release and a support KB entry explaining pin/mitigation and the root cause.

kevin_engineering: Will do. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/pull/4892 (WIP). Plan: reintroduce the idempotency generator and add a test that asserts the header exists on retries and the server receives a single effectful operation. If we can't ship immediate patch, we will cut a 1.26.1 hotfix.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-16T02:00Z: rolling canary to staging of redwood-python@1.26.1-candidate

maria_support: Action items for support: 1) advise affected customers to pin to `redwood-python==1.25.3` or set `REDWOOD_DISABLE_RETRIES=true` 2) collect customer request ids (X-Request-ID) where duplicates happened and attach to the ticket 3) escalate to billing team if double charges occurred and refund if confirmed.

sam_customer: Thanks — pin helped, and we enabled the header workaround while you patch. I'll DM our billing rep with the two request ids. Appreciate the fast help :heart:

kevin_engineering: Uploading unit test and quick fix in the PR, will request review from runtime team. ETA for hotfix cut: ~4 hours once CI passes.

maria_support: I'll prepare KB draft and a canned reply for support triage. Closing loop here but will update thread when patch is released.
